BiblicalUsage: White is the colour of manna, of clean garments, of leprosy, and of heaven's horses. In Exodus 16:31 the manna was white like coriander seed, in Ecclesiastes 9:8 the counsel is "let thy garments be always white," in Leviticus 13:3 the priest looks for hair turned white in the plague of leprosy, in Genesis 30:35 Jacob separates the sheep with white in them, and in Zechariah 1:8 the horses of the vision are white.
TheologicalSignificance: What I take from this is that white carries both meanings at once in Scripture: it is the colour of cleanness and of festivity, and also the mark the priest must read aright, because not every white is clean. The priest had to look twice, and so do I.
